response: {"headline": "IMPROVE-IT met its primary endpoint in 18,144 ACS patients, but the observed effect size and precision remain unknown at the 2014-11-17 cutoff, leaving the result consistent with a narrow success.", "summary": "The IMPROVE-IT trial (NCT00202878) randomized 18,144 acute coronary syndrome patients to ezetimibe/simvastatin versus simvastatin alone, with a primary endpoint of cardiovascular death, major coronary event, or non-fatal stroke. Merck announced on 2014-11-17 that the trial met its primary endpoint. A calculator using a -16.5% LDL-C change from a phase 2 familial hypercholesterolemia study (simvastatin 80 mg background) and an assumed baseline LDL-C of 2.0 mmol/L predicted a hazard ratio of 0.921 (7.9% relative risk reduction), but categorized the prediction as 'insufficient_data' because follow-up duration and event counts were unavailable. Human genetics published before cutoff (2014-11-12) showed NPC1L1 inactivating mutations associate with 12 mg/dL lower LDL-C and a protective odds ratio of 0.25-0.87 for coronary heart disease, supporting target and biomarker causality. The SHARP trial (9,270 patients, 1,145 events, 4.9-year median follow-up) demonstrated a hazard ratio of 0.83 (95% CI 0.74-0.94) for major atherosclerotic events with simvastatin/ezetimibe versus placebo, providing external mechanistic support.
